**Crowley** (Local pronunciation: ) is a city in, and the parish seat of, Acadia Parish in the U.S. state of Louisiana.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) At the 2020 United States census, Crowley had a population of 11,710.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-4) Crowley is the principal city of the Crowley micropolitan statistical area, which includes all of Acadia Parish. It is also part of the larger Lafayette–Acadianacombined statistical area.
Crowley was founded in 1886 by brothers C.C. "Curley" Duson and W.W. Duson. Curley Duson was sheriff of St. Landry Parish, of which the Crowley townsite was then a part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-5) Incorporated in 1887, W.W. Duson, General Manager of Southwest Louisiana Land Company, plotted and developed Crowley. W.W. Duson's daughter, Maime Duson, married Percy Lee Lawrence, who founded the First National Bank of Crowley. The 7-story building was once the tallest building between Houston and New Orleans.
The town was named after Patrick E. Crowley (1850-1909), an Irish-born employee of the Louisiana Western Rail Road.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-7) Crowley was in charge of a small facility nicknamed "Crowley's Switch" near Estherwood. The Dusons persuaded Crowley to move the switch about seven miles east to the Dusons' land in exchange for naming the town for him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-8)
According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of 5.85 square miles (15.2 km 2), all land.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-9)

Louisiana Highway 13 passes through the city with Kaplan, which is located in Vermilion Parish, being located 19 miles southeast and Eunice, located in both Acadia and St. Landryparishes, is located 20 miles north. The city of Rayne is located 9 miles east of Crowley via U.S. Highway 90 and I-10. The city of Jennings is located 17 miles west via U.S. Highway 90 and I-10.
Crowley has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen: Cfa) with long, hot summers and short, mild winters.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-10)

texts.1:
**Crowley** (Local pronunciation: ) is a city in, and the parish seat of, Acadia Parish in the U.S. state of Louisiana.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) At the 2020 United States census, Crowley had a population of 11,710.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-4) Crowley is the principal city of the Crowley micropolitan statistical area, which includes all of Acadia Parish. It is also part of the larger Lafayette–Acadianacombined statistical area.
Crowley was founded in 1886 by brothers C.C. "Curley" Duson and W.W. Duson. Curley Duson was sheriff of St. Landry Parish, of which the Crowley townsite was then a part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-5) Incorporated in 1887, W.W. Duson, General Manager of Southwest Louisiana Land Company, plotted and developed Crowley. W.W. Duson's daughter, Maime Duson, married Percy Lee Lawrence, who founded the First National Bank of Crowley. The 7-story building was once the tallest building between Houston and New Orleans.
The town was named after Patrick E. Crowley (1850-1909), an Irish-born employee of the Louisiana Western Rail Road.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-7) Crowley was in charge of a small facility nicknamed "Crowley's Switch" near Estherwood. The Dusons persuaded Crowley to move the switch about seven miles east to the Dusons' land in exchange for naming the town for him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-8)
According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of 5.85 square miles (15.2 km 2), all land.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-9)
texts.2:
Louisiana Highway 13 passes through the city with Kaplan, which is located in Vermilion Parish, being located 19 miles southeast and Eunice, located in both Acadia and St. Landryparishes, is located 20 miles north. The city of Rayne is located 9 miles east of Crowley via U.S. Highway 90 and I-10. The city of Jennings is located 17 miles west via U.S. Highway 90 and I-10.
Crowley has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen: Cfa) with long, hot summers and short, mild winters.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-10)

**Crowley** (Local pronunciation: ) is a city in, and the parish seat of, Acadia Parish in the U.S. state of Louisiana.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) At the 2020 United States census, Crowley had a population of 11,710.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-4) Crowley is the principal city of the Crowley micropolitan statistical area, which includes all of Acadia Parish. It is also part of the larger Lafayette–Acadianacombined statistical area.
Crowley was founded in 1886 by brothers C.C. "Curley" Duson and W.W. Duson. Curley Duson was sheriff of St. Landry Parish, of which the Crowley townsite was then a part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-5) Incorporated in 1887, W.W. Duson, General Manager of Southwest Louisiana Land Company, plotted and developed Crowley. W.W. Duson's daughter, Maime Duson, married Percy Lee Lawrence, who founded the First National Bank of Crowley. The 7-story building was once the tallest building between Houston and New Orleans.
The town was named after Patrick E. Crowley (1850-1909), an Irish-born employee of the Louisiana Western Rail Road.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-7) Crowley was in charge of a small facility nicknamed "Crowley's Switch" near Estherwood. The Dusons persuaded Crowley to move the switch about seven miles east to the Dusons' land in exchange for naming the town for him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-8)
According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of 5.85 square miles (15.2 km 2), all land.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-9)

Louisiana Highway 13 passes through the city with Kaplan, which is located in Vermilion Parish, being located 19 miles southeast and Eunice, located in both Acadia and St. Landryparishes, is located 20 miles north. The city of Rayne is located 9 miles east of Crowley via U.S. Highway 90 and I-10. The city of Jennings is located 17 miles west via U.S. Highway 90 and I-10.
Crowley has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen: Cfa) with long, hot summers and short, mild winters.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowley,_Louisiana#cite_note-10)
